text_blocks.snippet: Blood pressure of 130/80 mm Hg or higher is generally considered high blood pressure (hypertension).
Blood pressure is recorded as two numbers:

list.snippet: Systolic (top number): Pressure when your heart beats.
Diastolic (bottom number): Pressure when your heart rests between beats.

text_blocks.snippet: According to the American Heart Association and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the stages are:

snippet_links.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

list.snippet: Elevated: 120–129 systolic and less than 80 diastolic
Stage 2 Hypertension: 140 or higher systolic or 90 or higher diastolic
Hypertensive Crisis: Higher than 180 systolic and/or higher than 120 diastolic (requires immediate medical attention)

text_blocks.snippet: If you recently measured your blood pressure, would you like to share your reading numbers so I can tell you which category it falls into?
